content.title: 4/17/2026 Suns vs Warriors (Play-In Tournament) Game Preview | Phoenix Suns
content.text: Game 1 of this series was already a difficult task for the Suns after a quick turnaround from the play-in tournament. Couple that with the fact Oklahoma City is a generational defensive unit, and it was a perfect recipe for a tough Sunday.The Thunder took Game 1 in convincing fashion, defending homecourt with a 119-84 victory.Finding a way to win on the margins is Phoenix's path forward in this series. Unfortunately, that gameplan didn't yield positive results today as OKC won virtually every attainable margin. But two stood out the most: Turnovers and shot attempts.The Thunder weren't a team that prioritized offensive rebounding during the regular season. However, during Game 1, they won the possession game by collecting 19 offensive boards and forcing the Suns into 19 turnovers. With the Thunder being one of the most efficient teams in the league – and a nightmare to contain in transition – they will always take advantage of opponents' mistakes.OKC held the Suns to only two fastbreak points in this game, primarily keeping Phoenix in the halfcourt.On top of the havoc they create, Oklahoma City just never turns the ball over themselves. The Thunder finished with just six turnovers on their 93 possessions. The Suns' route to a competitive series is finding a way to increase that number and generating some easier chances for their own offense. It will be a tall order, though, because OKC simply doesn't beat itself.Devin Booker led the way for the Suns to begin his 10th playoff series in a Phoenix uniform. He scored 23 points on 8-of-17 shooting.Jordan Goodwin, who is a vital piece to Phoenix's approach and winning formula, had to exit the game in the first quarter with left calf soreness. He did not return to action.MVP favorite Shai Gilgeous-Alexander didn't have a strong shooting performance, only making five of his 18 field goal attempts, but he earned 17 trips to the foul line and helped OKC control the pace of the game.Phoenix has a couple of days to regroup, get some much-needed rest, and watch the film to pinpoint some adjustments. Game 2 in Oklahoma City will be Wednesday night at 6:30pm Pacific on ESPN.As head coach Jordan Ott mentioned after the game, Game 2 is a chance for the Suns to respond like they have all season. You flush this loss and aim for a split on the road.
